entries.mechanism: Reverified on PolicyEngine 4.18.9, PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, and PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The exact-household signature and explicit K-12 counterfactual reproduce the mechanism: PolicyEngine excludes all earnings of an imputed K-12 member age 17 or younger without requiring the co-resident-parent or parental-control condition in 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7). The sole minor is a valid household under 273.1(a)(1), but wages count under 273.9(b)(1)(i), so Axiom correctly fails the income gate and returns zero benefit. Requested-month regeneration retained exactly the same two case IDs and both paired eligibility rows. The two benefit rows materially changed from Axiom 0 / PolicyEngine 299.66998291015625 to Axiom 0 / PolicyEngine 298.0; the eligibility direction and lone-minor mechanism are unchanged.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 548.0 versus January PolicyEngine 535.2999877929688), and the unmodified direct requested-month simulation reproduces the same January value. Forcing the aggregate and state TANF inputs to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 548.5; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.5, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. The comparison bridge zeroes TANF on the Axiom input surface while PolicyEngine computes state TANF endogenously and counts it as SNAP unearned income (axiom-oracles#397 counterfactual class). Replay classifier record: class=tanf.

Disability-surface projection asymmetry, the SNAP analogue of the ssi-ecps disposition (axiom-oracles#228): the populace projection maps the Enhanced CPS is_disabled flag into Axiom's snap_member_is_elderly_or_disabled input (elderly_or_disabled transform in axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml), while PolicyEngine's SNAP elderly/disabled status (has_usda_elderly_disabled) requires receipt of a disability program, which the projected input surface zeroes. Axiom therefore applies the elderly/disabled treatment (gross-test exemption and uncapped excess-shelter deduction) while PolicyEngine does not. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values; the direct January simulation shows has_usda_elderly_disabled false while the persisted Axiom input surface carries the elderly/disabled flag for an under-60 member (1 cases / 2 rows).

Self-employment loss pass-through: the projection's flat 0.6 self-employment netting (axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml) passes Enhanced CPS self-employment losses through as negative Axiom earned income (sample ecps-67898: persisted snap_gross_monthly_earned_income -76562.87), while PolicyEngine floors SNAP self-employment income at zero (snap_self_employment_income_after_expense_deduction takes max(., 0)). Axiom's income tests pass on the loss-netted surface and it awards a benefit while PolicyEngine remains ineligible or lower. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values, and every selected row carries a negative Axiom earned-income input while the January PolicyEngine earned income is floored at or above zero (2 cases / 4 rows). A dedicated tracking issue for the self-employment-loss netting in the Populace bridge still needs filing; axiom-oracles#397 documents the same unequal-cross-program-input policy problem (same linkage as the fl-snap-ecps se-loss-netting class).

The comparison's PolicyEngine eligibility boolean comes from the batch output dataset's calendar-2026 aggregation, which reports eligible although the direct requested-month (2026-01) simulation is ineligible for January: the household fails the January income eligibility tests under the FY-2026 parameters while other 2026 months pass (income-limit uprating across the October fiscal-year boundary), and Axiom evaluates 2026-01 only. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the annual-aggregated True while the direct January simulation returns False on every selected row (4 rows; sample ecps-35744 January gross-income-to-poverty ratio 1.1422). The January benefit is zero on both engines, so only the eligibility boolean diverges — a harness period-aggregation artifact, not an engine defect.

Flat self-employment netting asymmetry: the generic populace projection feeds Axiom's snap_gross_monthly_earned_income with self-employment scaled by 0.6 (axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml documents the 0.6 scale as the oracle's modeled netting, calibrated against states with the 40-percent SNAP self-employment expense deduction), but Tennessee carries gov/usda/snap/income/deductions/self_employment rate 0 with the expense-based method in PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3, so PolicyEngine counts gross self-employment while Axiom receives 60 percent of it. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values, and January PolicyEngine SNAP earned income minus Axiom's persisted earned-income input equals 0.4x monthly self-employment within $1.00 on every selected row (17 cases / 20 rows; sample ecps-35304: 1623.3 - 973.98 = 649.32 = 0.4 x 1623.3). Benefit residuals reconcile as 0.3x the resulting net-income gap within the 30-percent rounding; eligibility flips occur where the gross-self-employment surface fails PolicyEngine's January income tests while the netted Axiom surface passes. A dedicated tracking issue for the flat self-employment netting in the Populace bridge still needs filing; axiom-oracles#397 documents the same unequal-cross-program-input policy problem (same linkage as the fl-snap-ecps se-expense-deduction-bridge class).
